newsitem.title: CANADA: Mitel shrs fall on removal from index.
newsitem.headline: Mitel shrs fall on removal from index.

text.p: Shares in Mitel Corp, battered by disenchanted investors for several weeks, continued to fall on Tuesday after getting an extra downward push from their removal from the Toronto Stock Exchange TSE 100 Index.

Mitel shares were down 0.30 to 7.25 on the TSE in heavy turnover of 2.06 million shares, up slightly from a 52-week low of 7.10 hit earlier. They were trading at 9.85 on February 21 when the major slide began.
In New York, the stock dipped 1/4 to 5-1/4 in quiet trade.
"I think there are two factors," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

"It was announced that Mitel would be removed from the 100 index effective March 21 in the morning. So I assume that some of the index players said 'there's no reason to own this thing anymore'," the analyst added.
He said the stock is also being pressured by investors' continued pessimism about the company's future after it last month warned it will take a C$13 million pre-tax charge.
Mitel told investors it will earn C$0.10 per share before the charge in the quarter, below analysts' expectations.
Traders said that further selling may be in the wind.
"I think some people might be tempted to pick up what looks like a bargain and I think that would be a mistake," the analyst said.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
